summary: Task 5 implements the four-file flip cleanly: UserService/EventService/EmailService return plain types, sendAsync preserves the silent-fire-and-forget contract via try/catch, and HttpRequestUtils consolidates the four duplicated extractors with byte-identical X-Forwarded-For semantics. USER_AGENT_MAX (500) matches both AuthService and ProjectController source-of-truth values, all referenced types (UserRepository, EventRepository, AppException, Event, User) resolve correctly, and no reactor.* imports remain under user/events/email. Two minor findings noted; no critical or major issues.

suggestions.suggestion: log.error logs only e.toString() (exception class + message), discarding the stack trace. Production debugging of MimeMessageHelper / MailException root causes is materially harder without it. Consider log.error("Email send failed to {}", to, e) so SLF4J appends the full stack. The spec (D15) pins the message template but leaves the throwable-arg open; passing the exception as the trailing throwable argument preserves the message format and adds the stack.
suggestions.benefit: Restores stack-trace-on-ERROR observability invariant noted in code-reviewing methodology ("Error logs include stack traces"). No change to the silent-fire-and-forget visible behaviour the spec mandates.

suggestions.suggestion: Mockito.lenient() on the User-Agent stub is unnecessary — the stub is invoked exactly once inside extractUserAgent. Strict stubbing would not flag it. Drop lenient() for consistency with the other tests in the same file that use plain when(...).thenReturn(...).
suggestions.benefit: Removes a non-load-bearing lenient() marker so reviewers don't assume there's a subtle reason for it.

suggestions.suggestion: Informational: the reactive original walked exchange.getRequest().getRemoteAddress().getAddress().getHostAddress(), so an unresolved InetSocketAddress would yield "unknown". The servlet form returns request.getRemoteAddr() (a String) and only falls back to "unknown" when that String is null. Tomcat/Jetty always populate getRemoteAddr() with a non-null IP string when available, so behaviour is equivalent in practice — but worth a one-line note in the Javadoc if a future reader wonders why we're not mirroring the reactive null-walk.
suggestions.benefit: Documents the intentional drop of the second null-guard so the next reader can quickly confirm no behavioural regression.
